title: Operator Workflow Trace Legacy Normalization
claim: FP-MCP-267 implemented legacy/manual operator workflow trace normalization in the MCP bridge summarizer, replacing UNKNOWN-only summaries for V0 manual trace artifacts with normalized deviation and side-effect counts.
summary: Updated the operator workflow trace summarizer to normalize both OPERATOR_WORKFLOW_TRACE_V1 records and earlier manual V0 trace artifacts with nested events arrays. The summarizer now expands legacy event entries, preserves root workflow metadata, counts event-level deviations, counts actual or declared side effects, lists tool mismatches, and adds review focus for missing or unrecognized deviation fields only when needed. Build and test passed, and a direct built-module validation against existing OPERATOR V0 traces returned four normalized events with WRONG_ADJACENT_TOOL_CALLED: 3 and UNEXPECTED_SIDE_EFFECT: 1.
caveats: This implementation was validated through build/test and direct built-module execution, but the running MCP service may need reload before the updated summarizer behavior is visible through ChatGPT MCP.
The packet does not change the writer schema and does not mutate historical V0 trace files.
The workspace inspection tool continued to display a path as rc/operator-workflow-trace.ts and staged status for raw M status; raw git status was used as source of truth.
boundaries: No OpenCode HTTP session was created.
No ForgePilot runner start endpoint was contacted.
No secrets or .env files were read.
Terminal was used only for repo inspection, source edit, build/test, direct module validation, and commit scaffolding.
